title: aiGateway + pdfService surfaces as consumed by visits.js, appointments.js, prescriptions.js — .NET 10 port recon

findings.name: aiGateway.chat(options) — the whole LLM surface
findings.signature: async chat({ system, user, model?, temperature?=0.3, maxTokens?=2000, useCache?=true, metadata?={} }) -> { text: string, provider: 'openai'|'gemini'|'micromind', model: string, tokensUsed: number|null, costUsd: number|null, cached: boolean }
findings.behaviour:
Only 3 of the 6 returned keys ever reach the client from these three route files: `text`, `provider`, `model`. `tokensUsed`, `costUsd` and `cached` are never surfaced by visits.js / appointments.js / prescriptions.js.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS (aiGateway.js:388-515):
1. Length guard FIRST, before cache, before audit: if `user.length > 50000` throws `Prompt too long (${user.length} chars, max 50000)`; if `system.length > 50000` throws `System prompt too long (${system.length} chars, max 50000)`. No audit row is written for either.
2. `inputHash = sha256(system + user)` (string concat, NOT JSON). This is the cache key too (`getCacheKey` exists but is dead code — never called).
3. If `useCache` (default true) and hit: returns `{...cachedResult, cached: true}` — the cached object carries the original `tokensUsed`/`costUsd`, but the audit row for the hit is written with `tokensUsed: 0, costUsd: 0`.
4. Provider chain walk. Each provider is SKIPPED (not attempted, no error recorded) when its env key is missing: openai needs OPENAI_API_KEY, gemini needs GEMINI_API_KEY, micromind needs AI_API_KEY.
5. Each attempt wrapped in `withRetry(fn, AI_MAX_RETRIES||2)` = 3 total attempts, delay `1000 * 2^attempt + random()*500`. Fail-fast (no retry) when `err.message.includes('Prompt too long')` or `err.status` in {400,401,403} or `err.code === 'invalid_api_key'`.
6. On total failure throws `AI Gateway: All providers failed. Last error: ${lastError?.message}`. QUIRK: if every provider was skipped for a missing key, `lastError` is null and the message is literally `AI Gateway: All providers failed. Last error: undefined`.

COST QUIRK: `costUsd: cost ? parseFloat(cost.toFixed(6)) : null` — a genuinely-zero cost (0 tokens) serialises as `null`, not `0`. Unknown model ⇒ `null`.

TIMEOUTS: OpenAI 30s (SDK option), Gemini 30s via `Promise.race` rejecting `Gemini timeout after 30s`, MicroMind 30s via AbortController.

MICROMIND PHI GUARD: `chatMicroMind` deliberately sends ONLY `{ question: user }` — the system prompt (which carries allergies/conditions/meds in generate-soap) is dropped. Returns `{ text: data.text || '', provider: 'micromind', model: 'micromind-agent', tokensUsed: null, costUsd: null }`. Any port must preserve this omission.
findings.portRecommendation: `IAiGateway.ChatAsync(AiChatRequest, CancellationToken) -> AiChatResult`. `AiChatResult` = `record(string Text, string Provider, string Model, int? TokensUsed, decimal? CostUsd, bool Cached)` with `[JsonIgnore]` irrelevant here since callers project manually. Model the total-failure case as a dedicated `AiGatewayUnavailableException` carrying the exact `AI Gateway: All providers failed. Last error: {msg|undefined}` string, because two endpoints (transcribe-rx, visits/transcribe) echo `err.message` straight into the 500 body. Owner: `Tebrazi.Ai` module, registered as a scoped service; the length guard, cache and provider chain belong inside the implementation, not in the route handlers — the handlers must stay ignorant of it exactly as they are in Node.

findings.name: AGENT_MODEL_DEFAULTS — the `model` field is dead code (routing quirk that changes the `aiModel` the client displays)
findings.signature: AGENT_MODEL_DEFAULTS: Record<agent, { provider, model }> — only `.provider` is read (line 443); `.model` is NEVER applied
findings.behaviour:
`agentConfig` is set only when `!model && metadata.agent && AGENT_MODEL_DEFAULTS[metadata.agent]`. Then `providerChain = dedupe([agentConfig.provider, primary, fallback, 'micromind'])`. `agentConfig.model` is never passed to the provider fn, so the actual model is always `process.env.OPENAI_MODEL || 'gpt-4o'` (openai) or `process.env.GEMINI_MODEL || 'gemini-2.0-flash'` (gemini). Defaults: `AI_PRIMARY_PROVIDER||'openai'`, `AI_FALLBACK_PROVIDER||'gemini'`.

What this means per call site in the three files:
- `agent:'soap'` (visits generate-soap, non-enhance) → chain ['gemini','openai','micromind'] → `aiModel` = GEMINI_MODEL||'gemini-2.0-flash'.
- `agent:'soap_enhanced'` (generate-soap with `enhance` truthy) → chain ['openai','gemini','micromind'] → `aiModel` = OPENAI_MODEL||'gpt-4o'.
- `agent:'icd_coder'` (visits suggest-codes) → gemini first.
- `agent:'drug_check'` (inside checkDrugs) → gemini first.
- `agent:'scribe'` (prescriptions transcribe-rx PARSE call, aiGateway.js line 425 maps scribe→{openai, whisper-1}) → chain starts 'openai' and calls `chatOpenAI` with `model=undefined` → gpt-4o, NOT whisper-1. The `whisper-1` in the table is inert; do not port it as a real model selection or the parse call breaks.
- `agent:'specialty_extract'` (generate-soap 2nd call; extract-from-plan) → NOT in the table → chain ['openai','gemini','micromind'].
- `agent:'scheduler'` (appointments ai-optimize) → NOT in the table → chain ['openai','gemini','micromind'].

The table is also keyed on `metadata.agent`, so passing an explicit `model` disables agent routing entirely — no call site in these three files passes `model`.
findings.portRecommendation: Port this as a `Dictionary<string, string>` of agent→**provider only** (`AgentProviderDefaults`), and deliberately drop the model column, with a comment that Node never applied it. If you port the `{provider, model}` pair faithfully and then *use* the model, `agent:'scribe'` starts sending `whisper-1` to the chat-completions endpoint and `/prescriptions/transcribe-rx` 500s. Config keys AI_PRIMARY_PROVIDER / AI_FALLBACK_PROVIDER / AI_MAX_RETRIES / AI_CACHE_TTL_MS must stay as-is.

findings.name: aiGateway.transcribe(options)
findings.signature: async transcribe({ audio: Buffer, language?: string, metadata?={} }) -> { text: string, duration: number, language: string, provider: 'openai', model: 'whisper-1', costUsd: number }
findings.behaviour:
OpenAI Whisper ONLY — no fallback chain, no cache. Throws `Transcription requires OPENAI_API_KEY (Whisper API)` synchronously (before any audit row) when the key is absent. `withRetry(fn, 1)` = 2 total attempts (note: 1, not the chat default of 2). 60s SDK timeout.

Mechanics that a port must mirror: the buffer is written to `os.tmpdir()/tebrazi_audio_${Date.now()}.webm`, streamed to the API, and `fs.unlinkSync`'d in a `finally`. Request is `response_format: 'verbose_json'` with a fixed medical-dictation `prompt` string (`'Medical clinical dictation. Patient presents with symptoms. Assessment, diagnosis, treatment plan, medications, follow-up.'`). `language` is set on the request ONLY if truthy — omitting it enables Whisper auto-detect.

RETURN QUIRKS:
- `duration` is Whisper's float seconds (e.g. `12.34`), defaulting to `0`. It is a Number in JSON, not a string.
- `language` is `transcription.language || language`. verbose_json returns the ENGLISH LANGUAGE NAME (`"english"`), not the ISO code the caller sent (`"en"`). The client at client/src/components/VoiceRecorder.jsx displays whatever comes back.
- `costUsd = parseFloat(((duration/60) * 0.006).toFixed(6))` — always a number here (unlike chat, no null branch).
- Audit rows are written with `tokensUsed: null` on success and `tokensUsed: 0, costUsd: 0, errorMsg: err.message` on failure, then the error is RE-THROWN.

Both call sites pass `language: req.body.language || 'en'`, so auto-detect is unreachable from these routes.
findings.portRecommendation: `IAiGateway.TranscribeAsync(byte[] audio, string? language, AiCallMetadata) -> AiTranscriptionResult(string Text, double Duration, string Language, string Provider, string Model, decimal CostUsd)`. `Duration` MUST be a floating-point type serialised without quotes. Do not 'fix' `Language` to return the ISO code — the client renders the value verbatim. Keep the missing-key failure as a distinct exception type whose `Message` is exactly `Transcription requires OPENAI_API_KEY (Whisper API)`, because both consuming endpoints leak `err.message` into their 500 body.

findings.name: aiGateway.checkDrugs(options) — the only surface with an internal, self-contained failure path
findings.signature: async checkDrugs({ drugs: string[], patientAllergies?=[], patientConditions?=[], metadata?={} }) -> { interactions: object[], drugsChecked: string[], message: string }
findings.behaviour:
EFFECTIVELY NEVER THROWS. Every failure mode is swallowed internally, which is why /check-interactions has no AI-failure branch of its own.

Pipeline:
- Guard: `drugs.length < 2` ⇒ immediate `{ interactions: [], drugsChecked: drugs, message: 'Need at least 2 drugs to check' }`. UNREACHABLE from prescriptions.js, which guards first with its own different message.
- Stage 1A `checkDrugsViaFDALabels`: for every unordered pair, GET `https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=drug_interactions:"A"+AND+drug_interactions:"B"&limit=2`. Per-pair try/catch (logs, continues). Pushes `{drug1, drug2, labelText, source:'fda_label'}` where labelText = concatenated first-300-char slices of matching sections, trimmed, capped at 600 chars.
- Stage 1B `checkDrugsViaFDAEvents`: `.../drug/event.json?...&limit=3`. Pushes `{drug1, drug2, eventCount, reactions: string[] (max 5), source:'fda_events'}`. `eventCount = data.meta?.results?.total || data.results.length`.
- Merge by `[drug1,drug2].sort().join('|')`: label rows win the base object and get `eventCount`/`reactions` grafted on (so a merged row keeps `source:'fda_label'`); event-only pairs are inserted as-is.
- Stage 2 runs ONLY if `mergedResults.length > 0 || patientAllergies.length > 0`. Calls `chat({...temperature:0.1, maxTokens:2000, useCache:FALSE, metadata:{...metadata, agent:'drug_check'}})`. Note useCache:false — drug checks are never cached.
- Parse: strips ```json / ``` fences, `JSON.parse`, `Array.isArray` check. **NO PER-FIELD SANITISATION** — whatever object shape the LLM emitted goes straight to the client. Contrast suggest-codes and ai-optimize, which both clamp/whitelist.
- Two identical degrade blocks (parse-failure at :689 and chat-throw at :701) map FDA rows to `{drug1, drug2, severity, description, recommendation:'Review patient history and monitor closely.', alternatives: []}` where `severity = source==='fda_label' ? 'MODERATE' : (eventCount>100?'HIGH':eventCount>20?'MODERATE':'LOW')` and `description = labelText || \`FDA reports ${eventCount || '?'} adverse events. Reactions: ${reactions.join(', ')}\``.
- Stage 3 string-match allergy scan (bidirectional substring, case-insensitive) appends `{drug1: drug, drug2: \`ALLERGY: ${allergy}\`, severity:'HIGH', description: \`Patient has a documented allergy to ${allergy}. ${drug} may cause an allergic reaction.\`, recommendation:'DO NOT prescribe. Consider alternatives.', alternatives: []}` unless the LLM already flagged that exact pair.
- Final order: `[...allergyWarnings, ...enrichedInteractions]` — string-match warnings are PREPENDED, not appended.
- `message`: `${n} interaction(s) found` or `'No known interactions detected'`.
- Audit row: `provider: mergedResults.length > 0 ? 'fda_label+llm' : 'llm_only'` (note: says llm_only even when the LLM threw), `model: null`, `inputHash = sha256(drugs.join(','))`, `tokensUsed: null, costUsd: null, success: true` ALWAYS.

If both allergies and FDA data are empty, Stage 2 is skipped entirely and the result is `{ interactions: [], drugsChecked: drugs, message: 'No known interactions detected' }` with an audit row claiming `provider:'llm_only', success:true` for a call that never happened.
findings.portRecommendation: `IAiGateway.CheckDrugsAsync(DrugCheckRequest) -> DrugCheckResult(IReadOnlyList<JsonElement> Interactions, IReadOnlyList<string> DrugsChecked, string Message)`. Because the LLM path is unsanitised, `Interactions` MUST be `List<JsonElement>` / `List<Dictionary<string,object?>>` — a strongly-typed `Interaction` record would silently drop or rename LLM-emitted keys and break the client. Provide a separate strongly-typed `FdaDegradedInteraction` record for the two degrade blocks only. Split the OpenFDA calls behind their own `IOpenFdaClient` so this can be stubbed independently of the LLM. Owner: `Tebrazi.Ai` module, but the OpenFDA client belongs in `Tebrazi.Integrations`.

findings.name: pdfService.generateRxPDFHtml(input) — returns an HTML STRING, never a PDF binary
findings.signature: generateRxPDFHtml({ clinic, physician, patient, prescription, medications }) -> string (a full <!DOCTYPE html> document). Synchronous, pure, no I/O. Sole export.
findings.behaviour:
NOT A PDF. Despite the filename, the route name `/pdf`, and the model field `pdfUrl`, this produces a print-ready HTML document with an inline `` and `@media print { @page { size: A4; margin: 12mm; } }`. The user makes the PDF via the browser print dialog. No PDF library is used or installed for this path. INPUT CONTRACT (only these properties are read): - `clinic`: `.logo` (optional img src), `.name`, `.address`, `.city`, `.phone` - `physician`: `.name`, `.specialty`, `.licenseNumber` - `patient`: `.name` only - `prescription`: `.signedAt`, `.createdAt`, `.id`, `.notes` only (the caller passes the whole entity; everything else is ignored) - `medications`: array of `{ drugName, dosage, frequency, duration, instructions }` DERIVED VALUES: - `rxDate = new Date(prescription.signedAt || prescription.createdAt).toLocaleDateString('en-GB', { day:'2-digit', month:'short', year:'numeric' })` - `rxNumber = prescription.id.slice(0, 8).toUpperCase()` — first 8 chars of the uuid (so it includes hex only, no dash, for a standard uuid). Will THROW TypeError if `id` were ever null. EMPTY-STATE RENDERING (all `escapeHtml(x) || 'fallback'` — see the escapeHtml finding): - `medications: []` ⇒ `\n \n ` (empty string joined), i.e. a header-only table, NOT a 'no medications' message. - Missing dosage/frequency/duration ⇒ literal em dash `—` (U+2014) per cell. - Missing drugName ⇒ `` (NO em dash — the `|| ''` after escapeHtml is dead code). - `med.instructions` falsy ⇒ the whole `
` is omitted (raw truthiness on the UNESCAPED value). - `clinic.name` falsy ⇒ literal `Clinic`. `clinic.logo`/`clinic.phone`/`physician.licenseNumber`/`prescription.notes` falsy ⇒ their whole element is omitted. - `[clinic.address, clinic.city].filter(Boolean).map(escapeHtml).join(', ')` — both null gives `

`. LITERAL NON-ASCII that must survive the port byte-identically: `℞` (U+211E) in `.rx-symbol`, `🖨` (U+1F5A8) in the print button, `—` (U+2014) in `Rx {n} — {physician}`, in every empty med cell, and in the footer `Generated by Tebrazi — Digital Healthcare Platform  |  tebrazi.com`. Signature line is `Electronically signed via Tebrazi · {rxDate}` with a middle dot U+00B7.
findings.portRecommendation: `IRxPdfRenderer.RenderHtml(RxRenderModel model) -> string` — name it `RenderHtml`, never `GeneratePdf`, and keep the return type `string`. `RxRenderModel` should be a flat DTO with exactly the 5 sub-objects above and nothing more, so the port cannot accidentally start rendering fields Node ignores. Implement with a raw interpolated string or a Razor-free template, NOT a templating engine that normalises whitespace/attribute order — the client writes the response into a new window via document.write, so whitespace differences are cosmetically safe but the byte-identity requirement makes a hand-written template the low-risk choice. Owner: `Tebrazi.Documents` module; it has zero dependencies (no DB, no HTTP), so it is trivially unit-testable against golden files.

findings.name: generateRxPDFHtml date formatting — 'Sept' (4 letters) and server-local timezone
findings.signature: new Date(signedAt||createdAt).toLocaleDateString('en-GB', {day:'2-digit', month:'short', year:'numeric'})
findings.behaviour:
Verified against the repo's Node v24.11.1 ICU: Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug **Sept** Oct Nov Dec. September renders as the FOUR-letter `Sept`, every other month as three letters. .NET's `DateTime.ToString("dd MMM yyyy", CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("en-GB"))` yields `Sep` — so a naive port produces `05 Sep 2026` where Node produces `05 Sept 2026`.

Second, and more consequential: `toLocaleDateString` with no timeZone option formats in the SERVER PROCESS timezone. The dev box resolves to `Africa/Cairo` (UTC+2/+3) with `TZ` unset. Prisma hands back a UTC `DateTime`, so a prescription with `signedAt = 2026-09-03T22:30:00Z` renders `04 Sept 2026`. The date appears TWICE in the document (patient bar `Date:` and the signature line), both from the same `rxDate` variable, so they always agree with each other.

The `|| createdAt` fallback means an unsigned DRAFT prescription still renders a date (its creation date) with no visual distinction from a signed one.
findings.portRecommendation: Do not use `MMM`. Implement a private `FormatRxDate(DateTime utc)` that converts to the configured server timezone (`TimeZoneInfo` from a config key, defaulting to the same zone the Node host runs in) and then formats via an explicit month-abbreviation array `["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sept","Oct","Nov","Dec"]` with `day.ToString("00")`. Cover all 12 months in a unit test. This lives inside `Tebrazi.Documents` next to the renderer.

findings.name: pdfService.escapeHtml — falsy-collapse quirk
findings.signature: function escapeHtml(str) { if (!str) return ''; return String(str).replace(/&/g,'&').replace(/</g,'<').replace(/>/g,'>').replace(/"/g,'"').replace(/'/g,'''); }
findings.behaviour:
Escapes in exactly this order: `&` first (so pre-existing entities get double-escaped: `&` in the source becomes `&amp;` in the output), then `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`→`'` (numeric, not `'`).

THE QUIRK: the `if (!str) return ''` guard is JS falsiness, so `escapeHtml(0)` returns the EMPTY STRING, not `"0"`. Same for `false`, `NaN`, `''`, `null`, `undefined`. A medication with `dosage: 0` renders as the em-dash fallback (because `'' || '—'`), and a numeric `0` anywhere renders blank. Verified by execution.

Consequence for the two `escapeHtml(x) || 'fallback'` idioms: the `||` never sees a raw null, only `''`, so the fallbacks (`'Clinic'`, `'—'`) fire on null AND on numeric zero AND on empty string alike. `escapeHtml(med.drugName) || ''` is therefore a no-op.
findings.portRecommendation: Write `static string Esc(object? v)` reproducing this exactly: return `""` for null, `""`, `0`/`0.0`/`false`/`NaN`, otherwise `v.ToString()` with the five replacements IN ORDER and `'` for the apostrophe. Do NOT use `System.Net.WebUtility.HtmlEncode` or `HttpUtility.HtmlEncode` — they emit `'` for apostrophe but differ on `"`/non-ASCII handling and do not double-escape existing entities the same way. Keep it private to `Tebrazi.Documents`.

findings.name: POST /api/visits/:id/generate-soap — AI SUCCESS response
findings.signature: router.post('/:id/generate-soap', aiUsageCheck('soap'), ...) — ai.chat at visits.js:757. Body: { enhance?: any, specialtyKey?: string }
findings.behaviour:
Success response, keys in this exact order:
```
{ message, subjective, objective, assessment, plan, aiProvider, aiModel, enhanced, aiUsage, specialtyData, specialtyKey }
```
- `message`: `'SOAP note generated with GPT-4o (enhanced). Review and edit as needed.'` when `enhance` is truthy, else `'SOAP note generated by AI. Review and edit as needed.'` (hard-coded 'GPT-4o' regardless of which provider actually answered).
- `subjective`/`objective`/`assessment`/`plan`: read back from the `prisma.visit.update` return, so they are the PERSISTED values — always strings, possibly `''`, never null after this call.
- `aiProvider`/`aiModel`: `result.provider` / `result.model` from the FIRST chat call only. The second (specialty-extract) call's provider is discarded.
- `enhanced`: `!!enhance` — a real boolean.
- `aiUsage`: `req.aiUsage || null` — see the aiUsageCheck finding for the Infinity→null hazard.
- `specialtyData`: `mergedSpecialtyData || null` — the FULL merged object (prior specialtyData + newly-extracted string values + `__templateKey`), or `null` if nothing was extracted. Never `{}`.
- `specialtyKey`: `activeTemplateKey || null`.

SOAP PARSING (visits.js after :757): regex `/(?:^|\n)\s*(SUBJECTIVE|OBJECTIVE|ASSESSMENT|PLAN)\s*:\s*/gi` over `result.text || ''`. If `markers.length >= 3`, each section is `text.substring(afterHeader, nextHeaderIndex).trim()`; a header the model omitted leaves that section as `''`. If `markers.length < 3` there is a SECOND, DIFFERENT fallback that still reports as AI success:
- `subjective = \`Patient presents with: ${visit.chiefComplaint || 'unspecified complaint'}\`` (NO trailing period — the template-fallback path below DOES have one)
- `objective = ''`
- `assessment = text.trim()`
- `plan = 'Review AI-generated assessment above and edit as needed.'`

PRE-AI GUARDS (all before the AI try block): 404 `{error:'Visit not found'}`; 403 `{error:'Not your visit'}` when no physicianProfile for req.user or `visit.physicianId !== physician.id`; 400 `{error:'No notes or transcript to process'}` when both `rawNotes` and `rawTranscript` are falsy. `source = visit.rawNotes || visit.rawTranscript || ''`.

PATIENT CONTEXT (injected into the system prompt, wrapped in its own bare `try {} catch {}`): loads `familySubprofile` with `allergies: true`, `conditions: {where:{isActive:true}}`, `medications: {where:{isActive:true}}` and formats 4 newline-joined lines — `Patient: {name} ({relation})`, `Allergies: {allergen} ({severity||'unknown'}), ...` or `'None documented'`, `Chronic Conditions: ...`, `Current Medications: {drugName} {dosage||''}`. Only when `visit.subprofileId` is set. Never reaches the response.

TEMPLATE DETECTION, 4-tier priority: (1) `req.body.specialtyKey` if it exists in SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES; (2) `visit.specialtyData.__templateKey` if valid; (3) heuristic — first template whose field keys overlap `Object.keys(specialtyData)` (excluding `__templateKey`) by `>= 2`, iterating SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES in declaration order and breaking on first match; (4) `getTemplateForSpecialty(physician.specialty)?.key` via the SPECIALTY_ALIASES lowercase-trim lookup.
findings.portRecommendation: One handler method; keep the DB write and the response projection in the handler, not in the gateway. Return an explicit DTO with `[JsonPropertyOrder]` matching the 11-key order above. `AiUsage` must be a nullable object property that serialises as JSON `null` (not omitted) when absent — use `JsonIgnoreCondition.Never` on that property. `SpecialtyData` must serialise as `null` (never `{}`). Implement the two distinct sub-fallbacks (marker-count < 3 vs. AI-threw) as separate private methods so the missing trailing period on the < 3 branch cannot be accidentally unified with the template branch. Owner: `Tebrazi.Api.Visits`.

findings.name: POST /api/visits/:id/generate-soap — the SECOND (nested, independently-degrading) ai.chat call
findings.behaviour:
Runs only when `activeTemplateKey` resolved AND `getFieldMapForPrompt(activeTemplateKey)` returned a non-empty string. Wrapped in its OWN `try/catch (extractErr)` that only logs — so a failure here does NOT trigger the outer template fallback; the endpoint still returns the AI-success shape with `specialtyData: null, specialtyKey: <key>`. This is the one nested degrade in the whole set.

Parsing: `rawExtract = (extractResult.text || '').trim()`, then `rawExtract.match(/\{[\s\S]*\}/)` (greedy — grabs from the first `{` to the LAST `}`, so trailing prose after the JSON breaks the parse), then `JSON.parse`. Parse failure logs a warning with a 200-char snippet and leaves `extractedData = null`.

MERGE (the important part): starts from `{...visit.specialtyData}` if it is a non-null object, else `{}`. For each extracted entry, skips `''`/null/undefined, otherwise `existing[key] = String(value)` — EVERY value is coerced to a string, so a numeric IOP of 14 is persisted as `"14"`. Only if `fieldsAdded > 0` does it set `existing.__templateKey = activeTemplateKey` and assign `mergedSpecialtyData`. There is NO whitelist against the template's field keys, so a hallucinated key is persisted verbatim.

`updateData` gets `specialtyData` ONLY when `mergedSpecialtyData` is truthy, so a failed extraction leaves the column untouched rather than nulling it. `getFieldMapForPrompt` (server/src/config/specialtyTemplates.js:500) builds a JSON-shaped string `{\n  "key": "Label [unit] (options: a, b)",\n  ...\n}`; `formatSpecialtyDataForPrompt` (:471) builds `--- {label} ---` / `[Section]` / `  {Label}: {value}{ ' '+unit}` lines and returns `''` when nothing is populated.
findings.portRecommendation: Model as a separate `ISpecialtyExtractor.TryExtractAsync(...) -> Dictionary<string,string>?` inside `Tebrazi.Api.Visits`, called from the SOAP handler and swallowing all exceptions. The string-coercion of every value is load-bearing for the client's form inputs — type it as `Dictionary<string, string>` so it cannot regress. Keep `__templateKey` as a magic string constant. Because it degrades silently, this call site is safe to ship against an AI stub that throws.

findings.name: POST /api/visits/:id/generate-soap — AI FAILURE response (template fallback)
findings.signature: catch (aiError) block — returns 200 with a 6-key body, five keys FEWER than the success shape
findings.behaviour:
Response, exact key order:
```
{ message: 'SOAP note generated (template — AI unavailable). Edit as needed.',
  subjective, objective, assessment, plan,
  aiProvider: 'template' }
```
MISSING vs. the success shape: `aiModel`, `enhanced`, `aiUsage`, `specialtyData`, `specialtyKey`. The client (client/src/pages/VisitDetailPage.jsx:215) reads them with `res.data.aiModel || null` and `if (res.data.specialtyData && typeof ... === 'object')`, so absence is tolerated — but a port that emits them as explicit `null`s changes the payload bytes. Note the em dash `—` in the message.

Generation (all four persisted via `prisma.visit.update` then read back):
- `lines = source.split('\n').filter(l => l.trim())` — n = lines.length, thirds via `Math.ceil(n/3)` and `Math.ceil(2n/3)`.
- `subjective = \`Patient presents with: ${visit.chiefComplaint || 'unspecified complaint'}.\n\nPatient reports:\n${firstThird.join('\n') || '(See raw notes)'}\`` — note the trailing PERIOD after the complaint, absent in the marker-count fallback.
- `objective = \`Physical examination findings:\n${middleThird.join('\n') || '(Pending examination documentation)'}\``
- `assessment = \`Clinical assessment:\n${lastThird.join('\n') || '(Pending clinical assessment)'}\``
- `plan = \`Treatment plan:\n- Follow-up as needed\n- ${visit.followUpNotes || 'Continue monitoring'}\``

SCOPE HAZARD: the `catch (aiError)` wraps the ENTIRE AI block INCLUDING the `prisma.visit.update`. A DB failure on the success path therefore silently reroutes into the template fallback and attempts the same update again. Only if that second update also throws does control reach the outer catch → 500 `{error:'Failed to generate SOAP note'}`.
findings.portRecommendation: This is the single most stub-friendly endpoint in the set: an `IAiGateway` that throws unconditionally yields a fully functional, deterministic, DB-persisting endpoint. Ship this on a stub. Implement the fallback as a pure `BuildTemplateSoap(Visit visit, string source)` function with a unit test on the thirds arithmetic (`Math.Ceiling` on integer division must be done in floating point: `(int)Math.Ceiling(n/3.0)`). Preserve the try-scope so a DB error re-enters the fallback — narrowing the catch would change behaviour.

findings.name: POST /api/visits/:id/transcribe
findings.signature: router.post('/:id/transcribe', upload.single('audio'), aiUsageCheck('scribe'), ...) — ai.transcribe at visits.js:983
findings.behaviour:
NO GRACEFUL DEGRADE. Any transcribe failure → 500 `{ error: error.message || 'Failed to transcribe audio' }`, LEAKING the internal message (e.g. `Transcription requires OPENAI_API_KEY (Whisper API)`).

Success response, exact key order:
```
{ transcript, duration, language, provider, fullTranscript }
```
- `transcript` = `result.text` (this recording only)
- `duration` = float seconds
- `language` = Whisper's language NAME (`"english"`), not the `"en"` that was sent
- `provider` = always `'openai'`
- `fullTranscript` = the accumulated column value. `result.model` and `result.costUsd` are NOT returned.

APPEND SEMANTICS: `existing = visit.rawTranscript || ''`; `separator = existing ? '\n\n--- New recording ---\n\n' : ''`; `updatedTranscript = existing + separator + result.text`. Persisted to `visit.rawTranscript`. Note: on the very first recording the separator is empty, so the marker appears only between recordings.

MIDDLEWARE ORDER: multer runs BEFORE `aiUsageCheck`, so a 429/403 from the limiter is returned only after the full audio body has been buffered into memory. multer config: `memoryStorage`, `fileSize: 25*1024*1024`, fileFilter accepting `['audio/webm','audio/mpeg','audio/wav','audio/mp4','audio/ogg','audio/x-m4a']` OR any `audio/*`, rejecting with `new Error('Only audio files are allowed')`.

Guards: 400 `{error:'No audio file provided'}` when `!req.file`; 404 `{error:'Visit not found'}`; 403 `{error:'Not your visit'}`. `language: req.body.language || 'en'`.
findings.portRecommendation: `IFormFile` + `[RequestSizeLimit(26214400)]`, and keep the filter/limiter ORDER (buffer then meter) if you want identical 429 timing. Useless without a real Whisper implementation — a stub can only produce the 500. If you must ship early, the honest stub is a 503 with a distinct message, and the client at client/src/components/VoiceRecorder.jsx:111 will surface it via `err.response?.data?.error`. Do not 'improve' the leaked `error.message`; the client displays it and it is currently the only signal that the key is unconfigured.

findings.name: POST /api/visits/:id/suggest-codes
findings.signature: router.post('/:id/suggest-codes', aiUsageCheck('icd10'), ...) — ai.chat at visits.js:1055, { temperature: 0.1, maxTokens: 1000, useCache: true, metadata: { agent:'icd_coder', visitId, userId } }
findings.behaviour:
TWO DIFFERENT FAILURE BEHAVIOURS — distinguish them carefully:
- ai.chat THROWS ⇒ outer catch ⇒ **500** `{ error: 'Failed to suggest diagnosis codes' }`. No degrade.
- ai.chat succeeds but the text does not parse ⇒ **200** `{ suggestedCodes: [], aiProvider, aiModel }`.

Success response is exactly 3 keys in this order: `{ suggestedCodes, aiProvider, aiModel }`. `suggestedCodes` is ALWAYS an array, never null, possibly empty. Nothing is persisted — this endpoint performs no writes.

SANITISATION PIPELINE (unlike checkDrugs, this one is strict): strip ```json / ``` fences → `JSON.parse` → `Array.isArray` guard → `.filter(c => c && c.code && c.description)` → map to EXACTLY `{ code, description, confidence }` where `code = String(c.code).toUpperCase().substring(0,10)`, `description = String(c.description).substring(0,200)`, `confidence = typeof c.confidence === 'number' ? clamp(c.confidence, 0, 1) : 0.5` → `.filter(c => !existingCodes.includes(c.code))` (dedupe AFTER uppercasing/truncating) → `.slice(0, 8)`. Any extra LLM keys are dropped. Note the prompt asks for 2-6 codes but the cap is 8.

PRE-AI: `soapContent = [assessment, plan, subjective, objective].filter(Boolean).join('\n')` — used ONLY for the 400 guard, never sent. 400 `{error:'No SOAP notes or chief complaint to analyze. Generate SOAP first.'}` when `!soapContent && !visit.chiefComplaint`. The prompt body sends chiefComplaint, assessment, plan and subjective (each defaulting to `'(Not documented)'`) but NOT objective.

`existingCodes = Array.isArray(visit.diagnosisCodes) ? visit.diagnosisCodes.map(c => c.code) : []` — an entry lacking `.code` contributes `undefined` to the array, which then never matches. These are injected into the system prompt as a do-not-repeat list only when non-empty.

Guards: 404 `{error:'Visit not found'}`, 403 `{error:'Not your visit'}`.
findings.portRecommendation: Strongly-typed `IcdSuggestion(string Code, string Description, double Confidence)` is safe here BECAUSE the handler already whitelists to those three keys. Return `{ suggestedCodes, aiProvider, aiModel }` in that order. `Confidence` must serialise as `0.5` (not `0.50`) for the default — use `double`, not `decimal`. NOT stub-viable in any useful sense: a throwing stub yields only a 500, and a stub returning empty text yields `{suggestedCodes: [], aiProvider: <fake>, aiModel: <fake>}` which the UI renders as 'no suggestions' — acceptable for a smoke test, useless as a feature.

findings.name: GET /api/appointments/ai-optimize — full stats shape and the stats-survive-AI-failure degrade
findings.signature: router.get('/ai-optimize', ...) — NO aiUsageCheck middleware. ai.chat at appointments.js:1492, { temperature: 0.2, maxTokens: 1200, useCache: true, metadata: { agent:'scheduler', userId } }
findings.behaviour:
THREE distinct 200-responses plus a 500. Note this route has NO usage-limiter middleware even though `'scheduler'` is in the PRO/CLINIC allowedAgents lists — so FREE-tier physicians reach it freely.

(a) NOT ENOUGH DATA — `allAppts.length < 5`: `{ stats: null, insights: [], message: 'Not enough appointment data for analysis. Need at least 5 appointments in the last 90 days.' }`. Has a `message` key the other shapes lack, and NO `aiProvider` key at all.
(b) AI SUCCESS: `{ stats, insights, aiProvider }`.
(c) AI FAILURE (`catch (aiError)` — logs and falls through): `{ stats, insights: [], aiProvider: null }`. `aiProvider` is assigned only AFTER the await resolves, so a throw leaves it `null`. Stats are fully preserved. This is the cleanest degrade in the set.
(d) Parse failure (chat OK, JSON bad): `{ stats, insights: [], aiProvider: '<real provider>' }` — distinguishable from (c) by a non-null aiProvider.
(e) 403 `{error:'Only physicians can access scheduling insights'}` if no physicianProfile; 500 `{error:'Failed to generate scheduling insights'}` from the outer catch.

`stats` object, EXACT key order (18 keys):
`totalAppointments`(int), `completed`(int), `noShows`(int), `cancelled`(int), `noShowRate`(float, 3dp via parseFloat(toFixed(3))), `cancelRate`(float 3dp), `completionRate`(float 3dp), `avgVisitDurationMin`(int or **null**), `avgSlotDuration`(int, defaults 30), `peakHour`(string `"HH:00"`), `busiestDay`(string day name or `'N/A'`), `avgDailyPatients`(float 1dp), `slotUtilization`(float 3dp capped at 1 via Math.min), `dayStats`(array), `hourDistribution`(array), `typeBreakdown`(object with DYNAMIC keys), `totalActiveSlotsPerWeek`(int), `analyzedDays`(int).
- `dayStats[]` = `{ day, dayIndex, total, noShowRate, cancelRate }` — day names from `['Sunday'..'Saturday']`, sorted by `total` DESC. Only days that actually have appointments appear.
- `hourDistribution[]` = `{ hour: "09:00", count }` sorted by `hour.localeCompare` (lexicographic).
- `typeBreakdown` = `{ IN_PERSON: n, ... }` keyed on `appointmentType || 'IN_PERSON'`, insertion-ordered by first occurrence.

`insights[]` (sanitised, max 6): `{ type, title, description, impact }` where `type` is whitelisted to NO_SHOW|SLOT_DURATION|PEAK_HOURS|UTILIZATION|CANCELLATION|THROUGHPUT else coerced to `'THROUGHPUT'`; `title = String(...).substring(0,120)` (prompt says max 80); `description = String(...).substring(0,500)`; `impact` whitelisted to HIGH|MODERATE|LOW else `'MODERATE'`. Pre-filter `.filter(i => i && i.type && i.title && i.description)`.

QUERIES: appointments `where {physicianId, appointmentDate: {gte: now-90d}}` selecting `id,status,appointmentDate,startTime,endTime,appointmentType,clinicId,cancelledAt,cancelReason` ordered `appointmentDate asc`; visits `where {physicianId, status:'COMPLETED', completedAt:{not:null}, visitDate:{gte:-90d}}` selecting `visitDate,completedAt`; timeSlots `where {physicianId, isActive:true}` selecting `dayOfWeek,startTime,endTime,slotDuration`. None of these apply a `deletedAt: null` filter, so soft-deleted appointments/visits ARE counted.

DERIVATIONS: `avgVisitDurationMin` = rounded mean of `(completedAt - visitDate)/60000` filtered to `> 0 && < 300`, or `null` if no visits or all filtered out. `totalCapacity = activeSlots.length * Math.ceil(90/7)` (=13 weeks). `avgDailyPatients = totalAppts / uniqueDays` to 1dp.
findings.portRecommendation: Return an explicit `AiOptimizeResponse` with `[JsonPropertyOrder]`, and model shape (a) as a SEPARATE DTO (`{stats, insights, message}`) so the `aiProvider` key stays absent rather than becoming `null`. `AvgVisitDurationMin` must be `int?`. `TypeBreakdown` must be `Dictionary<string,int>` preserving insertion order (use a `List<KeyValuePair>` or an ordered dictionary — .NET `Dictionary<,>` enumeration order is not contractual). Rates must serialise as 3-decimal-max floats without trailing zeros (`0.15`, not `0.150`) — `Math.Round(x, 3)` on a `double` gets this right in System.Text.Json. FULLY STUB-VIABLE and genuinely useful: the stats block is pure SQL, so an `IAiGateway` stub that throws gives a working analytics endpoint. Ship this first. Owner: `Tebrazi.Api.Appointments`.

findings.name: GET /api/appointments/ai-optimize — timezone and object-key-ordering hazards in the stats math
findings.signature: new Date(a.appointmentDate).getDay() / .toDateString(); byHour keyed on a.startTime?.split(':')[0]
findings.behaviour:
TWO silent-divergence traps, both verified by execution:

1. LOCAL-TIMEZONE DATE MATH. `new Date(a.appointmentDate).getDay()` and `new Date(a.appointmentDate).toDateString()` both evaluate in the SERVER PROCESS timezone (resolved `Africa/Cairo` on this host, `TZ` unset). Prisma returns UTC. So an appointment at `2026-09-06T22:00:00Z` (Sunday UTC) buckets into Monday, and `uniqueDays`/`analyzedDays`/`avgDailyPatients` count local calendar days. `dayStats[].day`, `dayStats[].dayIndex`, `busiestDay`, `analyzedDays` and `avgDailyPatients` are all affected. Also `ninetyDaysAgo = new Date(); setDate(getDate()-90)` keeps the current time-of-day, so the window boundary is a local wall-clock instant, not midnight.

2. `peakHour` TIE-BREAKING VIA JS OBJECT KEY ORDER. `byHour` is keyed on the two-char hour prefix of the `startTime` VARCHAR (`"09"`, `"14"`). `"14"` is an integer-like key and `"09"` (leading zero) is NOT, so V8's `Object.entries` emits integer-like keys first in ascending numeric order, THEN string keys in insertion order. Verified: `Object.entries({'14':2,'09':3})` → `[["14",2],["09",3]]`, and on a count tie `{'14':5,'09':5}` the stable sort yields `peakHour = "14"`, i.e. the AFTERNOON hour wins a tie against the morning one. `hourDistribution` is immune because it is explicitly `localeCompare`-sorted. If `startTime` is null the key is `'00'`; if `byHour` is empty `peakHour` defaults to `'09'`, giving `peakHour: "09:00"`.

`completedVisits` duration math uses `new Date(x).getTime()` differences, which are timezone-independent — that one is safe.
findings.portRecommendation: Convert to the configured server `TimeZoneInfo` explicitly before `DayOfWeek`/date-only bucketing; put the zone in one config key shared with the PDF renderer, and unit-test a 22:00Z appointment. For `peakHour`, reproduce the tie-break deliberately: build the counts into a `List<(string Hour, int Count)>` ordered as `keys.Where(IsIntegerLike).OrderBy(int.Parse)` then `keys.Where(!IsIntegerLike)` in insertion order, then `OrderByDescending(Count)` with .NET's stable `OrderBy`. Note .NET's `DayOfWeek` enum already has Sunday = 0, matching the `dayNames` array — no offset needed.

findings.name: POST /api/prescriptions/check-interactions
findings.signature: router.post('/check-interactions', ...) — NO aiUsageCheck. ai.checkDrugs at prescriptions.js:833. Body: { medications?: string[], subprofileId?, visitId? }
findings.behaviour:
NO AI-FAILURE BRANCH IN THE HANDLER, because `checkDrugs` never throws (see that finding). On total AI outage the endpoint still returns 200 with FDA-derived or string-match interactions. The only 500 is `{ error: 'Failed to check interactions' }` from a DB error.

Response, exactly 3 keys in order: `{ interactions, drugsChecked, message }`. NOTE: `drugsChecked` is the handler's own `allDrugs`, NOT `result.drugsChecked` — but `message` IS `result.message`. `interactions` is `result.interactions`, unsanitised LLM shapes and all.

EARLY RETURN (`allDrugs.length < 2`), also 3 keys but a different message: `{ interactions: [], drugsChecked: allDrugs, message: allDrugs.length === 0 ? 'No active medications found' : 'Only 1 active medication found — no interactions to check' }`. Em dash U+2014 in the second string. This shadows checkDrugs' own `'Need at least 2 drugs to check'`, which is unreachable from here.

DRUG-LIST ASSEMBLY (four sources, order matters for `drugsChecked`):
1. `inputMeds` = `req.body.medications` filtered truthy (client sends bare strings).
2. `currentMedication where {subprofileId, isActive:true}` → drugName, only if `subprofileId` given.
3. Cross-prescription: `patientUserId` comes from `visit.patientUserId` when `visitId` given, ELSE from `req.user.id` when `req.user.userType !== 'PHYSICIAN'` (so a physician calling with no visitId gets no cross-Rx data). Then `prescription where { visit: { patientUserId }, status: { in: ['SIGNED','CONFIRMED','SENT','DISPENSED'] } }` selecting `medications`; for each, `rx.medications.filter(m => !m.stoppedAt).map(m => m.drugName || m).filter(Boolean)`. QUIRK: this tolerates BOTH object entries and bare-string entries — for a string, `m.stoppedAt` is undefined so it always passes the stopped filter, and `m.drugName || m` yields the string itself. No `deletedAt` filter, so soft-deleted prescriptions contribute drugs.
4. If `!subprofileId`, ALL subprofiles of that patient are walked in an N+1 loop pulling their active currentMedications.
Final: `allDrugs = [...new Set([...inputMeds, ...existingDrugs].filter(Boolean))]` — insertion-ordered dedupe, input meds first. Case-sensitive dedupe, so 'Aspirin' and 'aspirin' both survive.

ALLERGY/CONDITION CONTEXT (bare `try {} catch {}`): `subId = subprofileId || (first familySubprofile of patientUserId)?.id` — QUIRK: for a multi-subprofile family with no subprofileId, this picks an ARBITRARY subprofile's allergies. Then parallel `allergy where {subprofileId: subId, isActive:true} select allergen` and `chronicCondition where {..., isActive:true} select name` → `patientAllergies: string[]`, `patientConditions: string[]`.

SIDE EFFECT (own try/catch, logs on failure): `interactionAlert.create({ physicianId: physician?.id || null, patientUserId: !physician ? req.user.id : null, drugs: allDrugs, interactions: result.interactions, alertCount: result.interactions.length })`. QUIRK: `visitId` is NOT written even though the model has the column and `req.body.visitId` is in hand. Also `physicianId` and `patientUserId` are mutually exclusive — a physician's check never records the patient.
findings.portRecommendation: `Interactions` must be `List<JsonElement>` (see the checkDrugs finding). Keep the two 3-key shapes as one DTO with a settable `Message`. The bare-string-vs-object medication handling in source 3 needs an explicit `JsonElement.ValueKind` switch in C# — a typed `List<MedicationDto>` deserialise will throw on the string form. Preserve the omitted `VisitId` on the InteractionAlert insert (or fix it as a separate, flagged change — it alters DB content, not JSON). FULLY STUB-VIABLE: with `IOpenFdaClient` returning empty and `IAiGateway` throwing, the endpoint still returns real string-match allergy warnings, which is clinically the most important half. Ship on a stub. Owner: `Tebrazi.Api.Prescriptions`, with the drug-list assembly extracted to a testable `DrugListAssembler`.

findings.name: GET /api/prescriptions/:id/pdf — returns text/html, NOT a PDF binary; no Content-Disposition
findings.signature: router.get('/:id/pdf', ...) — generateRxPDFHtml at prescriptions.js:925; res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/html') at :939; res.send(html) at :940
findings.behaviour:
HEADERS — the answer to the explicit question:
- `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`. The handler sets only `text/html`, but Express 4.22.1 `res.send(string)` appends the charset (verified in node_modules/express/lib/response.js: for a string chunk it does `this.set('Content-Type', setCharset(type, 'utf-8'))` when a type is already present). A .NET port that returns bare `text/html` is NOT byte-identical on the wire.
- **NO Content-Disposition header is set anywhere.** Not `inline`, not `attachment`, no filename. The response renders inline.
- `Content-Length` and a STRONG `ETag` are added by Express (`app.set('etag','strong')` at server/src/index.js:39), and `compression()` (:36) may gzip it.
- `helmet()` (:33) adds its defaults, including `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a CSP with `script-src 'self'; script-src-attr 'none'`. This matters: client/src/pages/VisitInboxPage.jsx:147 does `window.open('/api/prescriptions/${rxId}/pdf','_blank')`, loading the document DIRECTLY under that CSP, where `script-src-attr 'none'` BLOCKS the inline `onclick="window.print()"` — the Print button is inert on that path. The other two call sites (client/src/components/PrescriptionPanel.jsx:207 and client/src/pages/PrescriptionsPage.jsx:234) fetch with `responseType:'text'` and `document.write` into a blank window, where the API's CSP does not apply and the button works.

No DB write — `pdfUrl` is never populated by this endpoint.

PRISMA INCLUDE, expanded to the literal object the handler holds: all Prescription scalars (`id, visitId, physicianId, subprofileId, status, medications, notes, signedAt, sentToPatientAt, pdfUrl, refillRequestedAt, refillStatus, refillNotes, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt`) plus `visit: { patientUserId, clinicPatientId, clinicPatient: { name } | null, clinic: { name, address, city, phone, logo } }`, `physician: { specialty, licenseNumber, user: { displayName } }`, `subprofile: { name, relation } | null`. None of this is serialised to JSON — it all feeds the template.

QUIRK: `findUnique` with NO `deletedAt: null` filter, so a soft-deleted prescription still renders. Also no `status` gate — a DRAFT renders identically to a SIGNED one (only the date differs, via the `signedAt || createdAt` fallback).

ACCESS CHECK: `isPhysician = physician && prescription.physicianId === physician.id`; `isPatient = prescription.visit.patientUserId === req.user.id`; neither ⇒ 403 JSON `{error:'Access denied'}`. Clinic staff and other physicians in the same clinic are refused.

PATIENT NAME RESOLUTION, in this priority: (1) `subprofile` present ⇒ `\`${subprofile.name} (${subprofile.relation})\`` — relation is the raw enum token, e.g. `SELF`, `SPOUSE`; (2) `visit.clinicPatient?.name`; (3) an EXTRA `user.findUnique` for `visit.patientUserId` → `displayName`; (4) literal `'Patient'`.

ARGUMENTS PASSED: `clinic: prescription.visit.clinic || { name: 'Clinic' }` (defensive; `clinic` is a required relation so the fallback is effectively dead), `physician: { name: physician.user.displayName, specialty: physician.specialty || '', licenseNumber: physician.licenseNumber || '' }` (both are non-null Strings in the schema, so `|| ''` only fires on stored empty strings), `patient: { name: patientDisplayName }`, `prescription` (whole entity), `medications: Array.isArray(prescription.medications) ? prescription.medications : []`.

Errors: 404 `{error:'Prescription not found'}`, 403 `{error:'Access denied'}`, 500 `{error:'Failed to generate PDF'}`.
findings.portRecommendation: `return Content(html, "text/html", Encoding.UTF8)` — this produces `text/html; charset=utf-8`, matching Express. Do NOT add a Content-Disposition, and do NOT switch to a real PDF: three client call sites treat the body as HTML text, and one of them `document.write`s it. Keep `app.UseResponseCompression()` and strong ETags on to match headers. Interface: `IRxPdfRenderer.RenderHtml(RxRenderModel)` — the handler owns the include/projection and the name-resolution ladder, the renderer stays pure. NEEDS NO AI AT ALL, so it ships complete on day one independently of `IAiGateway`. Owner: handler in `Tebrazi.Api.Prescriptions`, renderer in `Tebrazi.Documents`.

findings.name: POST /api/prescriptions/transcribe-rx — two chained AI calls, degrades on ONE of the two failure modes only
findings.signature: router.post('/transcribe-rx', rxUpload.single('audio'), aiUsageCheck('scribe'), ...) — ai.transcribe at prescriptions.js:989, then ai.chat at :1001 { temperature: 0.1, maxTokens: 1000, metadata: { agent:'scribe', context:'rx_parse', userId } }
findings.behaviour:
THE CRITICAL ASYMMETRY: the handler degrades gracefully when the parse-step's JSON is unreadable, but NOT when either AI call THROWS. A `chat` throw lands in the outer catch and the transcript — already paid for and successfully produced — is DISCARDED.

Four outcomes:
(a) Both calls succeed, JSON parses ⇒ 200 `{ transcript, medications, transcribeDuration }` (3 keys, that order). `transcribeDuration` is `transcribeResult.duration` (float seconds) and is the ONLY place the duration surfaces; the client ignores it.
(b) chat succeeds, JSON does NOT parse ⇒ 200 `{ transcript, medications: [], parseError: 'Could not parse medications from transcript. Please add them manually.' }` — 3 keys, but `transcribeDuration` is REPLACED by `parseError`. The client (client/src/components/PrescriptionPanel.jsx:70-90) branches on `res.data.parseError` to show a message. A port MUST NOT emit both keys.
(c) EITHER call throws ⇒ 500 `{ error: error.message || 'Failed to transcribe prescription' }` — leaks internals verbatim: `Transcription requires OPENAI_API_KEY (Whisper API)`, `AI Gateway: All providers failed. Last error: undefined`, or `Prompt too long (N chars, max 50000)`.
(d) Transcript too short ⇒ 400 `{ error: 'Could not transcribe audio. Please try again.' }` when `!transcript || transcript.trim().length < 3`.

MEDICATION SANITISATION (strict, unlike checkDrugs): strip ```json / ``` fences → `JSON.parse` → `Array.isArray` guard → `.filter(m => m && m.drugName)` → map to EXACTLY `{ drugName, dosage, frequency, duration, instructions }`, each `String(m.x || '').trim()`. Every field is a string, never null; absent fields become `''`. No cap on array length. Extra LLM keys dropped. The `forms: []` key the client adds is client-side only.

No DB write of any kind — this endpoint is read-only apart from the audit rows inside the gateway.

Guards: 400 `{error:'No audio file provided'}`; 403 `{error:'Only physicians can dictate prescriptions'}` when no physicianProfile. multer: `memoryStorage`, 25MB, fileFilter accepts only `file.mimetype.startsWith('audio/')` (STRICTER than visits.js, which also has an explicit allowlist) and rejects with `new Error('Only audio files are allowed')`. `language: req.body.language || 'en'`.
findings.portRecommendation: Model the response as a union, not one nullable-rich DTO: `TranscribeRxSuccess(string Transcript, List<MedicationDto> Medications, double TranscribeDuration)` and `TranscribeRxParseFailed(string Transcript, List<MedicationDto> Medications, string ParseError)` — emitting both `transcribeDuration` and `parseError` in one payload would be a new shape the client has never seen. `MedicationDto` is safely strongly-typed (5 non-null strings) because the handler whitelists. USELESS WITHOUT A REAL IMPLEMENTATION: it needs both Whisper and a chat model, and there is no non-500 degraded path. Deprioritise; if a stub must exist, have it throw so at least the 500 shape is exercised. Consider (as a flagged behaviour change, not a port) returning the transcript on chat-throw — but do not do it silently.

findings.name: POST /api/prescriptions/extract-from-plan
findings.signature: router.post('/extract-from-plan', ...) — NO aiUsageCheck. ai.chat at prescriptions.js:1092 { temperature: 0.1, maxTokens: 1000, useCache: FALSE, metadata: { agent:'specialty_extract', userId } }. Body: { planText: string }
findings.behaviour:
The narrowest surface: the response is ONE key, always. `{ medications }` — never null, always an array, possibly empty. `aiProvider`/`aiModel` are NOT returned here (unlike suggest-codes), so the client cannot tell a real extraction from a degraded one.

Failure split:
- ai.chat THROWS ⇒ outer catch ⇒ **500** `{ error: 'Failed to extract medications' }`. No degrade. (The internal message is NOT leaked here, unlike transcribe-rx.)
- chat OK but no `[...]` match, or JSON.parse throws ⇒ **200** `{ medications: [] }`. The client (client/src/components/PrescriptionPanel.jsx:277) treats an empty array as `setError('No medications found in the Plan text')`, so a silent AI degradation is indistinguishable from a plan with no drugs in it.

PARSING: `result.text.match(/\[[\s\S]*\]/)` — greedy, first `[` to LAST `]`, so trailing prose breaks it. Then the SAME 5-field sanitisation as transcribe-rx: `.filter(m => m && m.drugName)` → `{ drugName, dosage, frequency, duration, instructions }` each `String(m.x || '').trim()`. Note `useCache: false` here, versus the cached default in suggest-codes/ai-optimize — identical plan text re-hits the model every time.

Guards: 400 `{error:'Plan text is required'}` when `!planText || planText.trim().length < 5`; 403 `{error:'Only physicians can extract prescriptions'}` when no physicianProfile. No DB write. `logger.info({count})` on the way out.
findings.portRecommendation: `ExtractFromPlanResponse(List<MedicationDto> Medications)` — reuse the same `MedicationDto` as transcribe-rx; the two sanitisation blocks are byte-identical and should be one shared `SanitizeMedications(JsonElement)` helper in `Tebrazi.Api.Prescriptions`. Set `useCache: false` explicitly on the gateway call. STUB-VIABLE ONLY DEGENERATELY: a stub returning empty text gives `{medications: []}` at 200, which the UI reports as 'no medications found' — technically shippable, functionally dead. Rank it with suggest-codes: needs a real model to be worth anything.

findings.name: aiUsageCheck middleware — the Infinity→null JSON hazard, and which endpoints it guards
findings.signature: aiUsageCheck(agentName) -> express middleware; sets req.aiUsage = { used, limit, remaining, tier }
findings.behaviour:
THE QUIRK, verified by execution: for the CLINIC tier `req.aiUsage = { used: 0, limit: Infinity, remaining: Infinity, tier: 'CLINIC' }`, and `JSON.stringify` turns both Infinities into **`null`**. So generate-soap's `aiUsage` field reaches a CLINIC-tier client as `{"used":0,"limit":null,"remaining":null,"tier":"CLINIC"}`. A .NET `double.PositiveInfinity` THROWS in System.Text.Json by default; `int?` with null is the byte-identical port.

APPLIED TO (only these, in the three files): `visits.js` generate-soap (`'soap'`), visits.js transcribe (`'scribe'`), visits.js suggest-codes (`'icd10'`), prescriptions.js transcribe-rx (`'scribe'`). NOT applied to: `/appointments/ai-optimize` (despite `'scheduler'` being a tiered agent), `/prescriptions/check-interactions` (despite `'drug_check'` being one), `/prescriptions/extract-from-plan`, `/prescriptions/:id/pdf`.

BLOCKING RESPONSES (returned INSTEAD of the handler, so the client sees a completely different shape):
- 401 `{error:'Authentication required'}` if no req.user.id; 401 `{error:'User not found'}`.
- 403 `{ error: 'Feature not available on your plan', message: \`The ${formatAgentName(agent)} feature requires a Pro subscription.\`, upgradeRequired: true, currentTier }`. `formatAgentName` maps soap→'AI SOAP Generator', icd10→'ICD-10 Auto-Coder', scribe→'Medical Scribe', drug_check→'Drug Interaction Checker', etc., falling through to the raw agent name.
- 429 `{ error: 'Monthly AI limit reached', message: \`You've used ${used}/${limit} AI calls this month. Upgrade to Pro for more.\`, upgradeRequired: true, currentTier, usage: { used, limit, totalTokens, totalCost, resetsAt: <ISO string of next month start, LOCAL-tz-derived> } }`.
- FAIL-OPEN: any thrown error in the middleware calls `next()` and leaves `req.aiUsage` UNDEFINED, so generate-soap emits `aiUsage: null`. Deliberate ('fail-open for clinical safety').

TIER GATES relevant here: PATIENT_FREE/PATIENT_FAMILY allow ONLY `health_chat`, so any patient hitting generate-soap/transcribe/suggest-codes/transcribe-rx gets the 403 upgrade shape. FREE allows soap/icd10/scribe/cds/drug_check/clinic_ai/clinical_reference at 50 calls/mo but NOT scheduler. Counting: `aiAuditLog.aggregate` over `{userId, createdAt >= monthStart(local), success: true, cached: false}` — cached calls are free.

RACE: the gateway's `logAudit` is FIRE-AND-FORGET (not awaited) in both `chat` and `transcribe`, so the count the middleware reads can lag the calls just made, and generate-soap's TWO chat calls both write rows against one metered request.
findings.portRecommendation: An `[AiUsage("soap")]` action filter writing to `HttpContext.Items`. `AiUsageDto` must be `(int Used, int? Limit, int? Remaining, string Tier)` with Limit/Remaining `null` for CLINIC — never `double.PositiveInfinity`. Keep the fail-open catch. Keep the audit write fire-and-forget (`_ = Task.Run(...)` with its own try/catch, or a channel) so the metering race is reproduced rather than accidentally tightened. `resetsAt` uses `new Date(year, month+1, 1).toISOString()` — a LOCAL-midnight instant rendered as UTC, so port it via the same server TimeZoneInfo, not `DateTime.UtcNow`.

findings.name: AiAuditLog write shape and cache semantics — the DB side-effects a port must reproduce
findings.signature: logAudit({ agent, provider, model, userId, inputHash, tokensUsed, costUsd, latencyMs, success, errorMsg, cached, metadata }) — awaited nowhere except inside its own try/catch; swallows all errors
findings.behaviour:
Rows are written ONLY when `metadata.userId` is present. Every call site in the three route files passes `userId`, so every call is logged. `metadata` is stored WHOLE as JSON, including the duplicated `agent` and `userId` — e.g. generate-soap writes `{"agent":"soap","visitId":"<uuid>","userId":"<uuid>"}`; ai-optimize writes `{"agent":"scheduler","userId":"..."}`; transcribe-rx's two calls write `{"agent":"scribe","context":"prescription_dictation","userId":...}` and `{"agent":"scribe","context":"rx_parse","userId":...}`. `checkDrugs` writes a DIFFERENT metadata for its inner chat (`{...metadata, agent:'drug_check'}`) than for its own summary row.

Per-outcome column values:
- cache hit: `tokensUsed: 0, costUsd: 0, cached: true, success: true`, provider/model from the CACHED result.
- chat success: real `tokensUsed`/`costUsd` (which may be `null`), `cached: false, success: true`.
- chat total failure: `provider: 'none', model: null, tokensUsed: 0, costUsd: 0, success: false, errorMsg: lastError?.message || 'All providers failed'`.
- transcribe success: `provider:'openai', model:'whisper-1', tokensUsed: null`, real costUsd.
- transcribe failure: same provider/model, `tokensUsed: 0, costUsd: 0, errorMsg: err.message`, then RE-THROWS.
- checkDrugs summary: `agent:'drug_check', provider: mergedResults.length>0 ? 'fda_label+llm' : 'llm_only', model: null, tokensUsed: null, costUsd: null, success: TRUE always`, `inputHash = sha256(drugs.join(','))`.
No row at all for the prompt-length rejections.

CACHE: process-local `Map`, keyed on `sha256(system + user)`, TTL `AI_CACHE_TTL_MS || 3600000`, max 200 entries, true LRU (get re-inserts to move to the tail; set deletes-then-inserts), plus a 5-minute `setInterval(...).unref()` sweep. Consequences the port inherits: cached responses can be MINUTES-TO-AN-HOUR stale, cache hits do not count against the monthly quota, and the cache is per-process (so it does not survive a restart and is not shared across instances). suggest-codes and ai-optimize use it; check-interactions and extract-from-plan explicitly opt out with `useCache: false`; generate-soap and the transcribe-rx parse call use the default (cached).
findings.portRecommendation: `IAiAuditLog.WriteAsync(AiAuditEntry)`, called fire-and-forget from inside the gateway, swallowing all exceptions — never from a route handler. `TokensUsed`/`CostUsd` must be `int?`/`decimal?` so the null-vs-0 distinction per outcome survives. `Metadata` should be `Dictionary<string,object?>` serialised as-is, duplicated `agent`/`userId` included. For the cache, `IMemoryCache` with `SizeLimit = 200` gets you eviction but NOT LRU-on-read; if the staleness/quota behaviour matters, write a small explicit LRU. Do NOT move the cache to Redis as part of the port — a shared cache changes which requests are billed and metered. Owner: `Tebrazi.Ai`.

findings.name: Stub-viability matrix for the .NET port
findings.behaviour:
Which of the eight AI/PDF endpoints in these three files can ship against a throwing `IAiGateway` stub, based on the degrade paths documented above.

SHIP NOW, NO AI NEEDED AT ALL:
1. `GET /api/prescriptions/:id/pdf` — zero AI. Needs only `IRxPdfRenderer`. Fully functional day one.

SHIP ON A THROWING STUB, GENUINELY USEFUL:
2. `GET /api/appointments/ai-optimize` — the 18-key `stats` block is pure SQL; the AI catch leaves `{stats, insights: [], aiProvider: null}`. The analytics dashboard works.
3. `POST /api/visits/:id/generate-soap` — the `catch (aiError)` template fallback persists real SOAP text and returns the documented 6-key `aiProvider:'template'` body. Deterministic and testable.
4. `POST /api/prescriptions/check-interactions` — `checkDrugs` cannot throw; with OpenFDA stubbed empty and the LLM down it still returns the Stage-3 string-match allergy warnings, which is the highest-value half of the feature clinically.

SHIP ON A STUB ONLY DEGENERATELY (200 with empty results; feature is dead but nothing 500s) — requires the stub to return EMPTY TEXT rather than throw:
5. `POST /api/visits/:id/suggest-codes` — empty text ⇒ 200 `{suggestedCodes: [], aiProvider, aiModel}`. A throwing stub gives 500 instead.
6. `POST /api/prescriptions/extract-from-plan` — empty text ⇒ 200 `{medications: []}`, which the UI reports as 'No medications found in the Plan text'. A throwing stub gives 500.

USELESS WITHOUT A REAL IMPLEMENTATION — no non-500 degraded path exists:
7. `POST /api/visits/:id/transcribe` — needs Whisper. Any failure is 500 `{error: <leaked message>}`.
8. `POST /api/prescriptions/transcribe-rx` — needs Whisper AND a chat model; a chat throw discards the transcript and 500s. Its only graceful path (`parseError`) requires a chat call that SUCCEEDS with unparseable text.

Also note the one nested degrade: generate-soap's specialty-extract call (visits.js:822) has its own catch, so it never affects endpoint viability.
findings.portRecommendation: Register two distinct stubs, not one: `ThrowingAiGateway` (drives #2/#3/#4 down their real degrade paths — use it for integration tests) and `EmptyTextAiGateway` (returns `{ Text: "", Provider: "stub", Model: "stub", ... }`, needed to make #5/#6 return 200). Sequence the port as: #1 → #2 → #3/#4 → #5/#6 → #7/#8 last, since the audio endpoints need the temp-file + multipart + Whisper plumbing that nothing else shares. Golden-file tests against the Node responses are cheap for #1/#2/#3 and should be written first — those three carry the most quirks (Sept/timezone, peakHour tie-break, the 6-vs-11 key fallback shape).
